description:
Found by the fz-kdt.198 refutation (2026-09-03). PRE-EXISTING: measured
identical at accb5cfbe and at fz-kdt.198's c1f7a7d1b, so 198 neither causes
nor worsens it -- but it FALSIFIES the sentence 198 wanted to write ("brands
are erased before the backend"), which is why it is written down here.

MEASURED. .kdt198/refute/a1_two_activations.fz:

    import Utf8
    @spec pass(a) :: a
    fn pass(x), do: x
    fn main() do
      s = Utf8.from_bytes!(<<104, 105>>)
      b = <<106, 107>>
      dbg(Utf8.to_bytes(pass(s)))
      dbg(pass(b))
    end

`fz2 interp --dump backend=...` gives TWO activations of one body:

    key pass/1[fp[binary;nutf8] utf8(binary)] need=Value
    key pass/1[fp[binary] binary]             need=Value

(at accb5cfbe the same two keys, the second field rendering `binary | utf8`).
The `brand_refines_its_inner.fz` dump carries 29 `utf8` tokens.

WHY IT IS WRONG. `TyCanon::descr_fingerprint` records the brand slot as the
`n` component, and the fingerprint is what keys the activation. A brand is a
TYPING refinement with no runtime witness: `Types::runtime_type_predicate`
never reads the slot (set-theoretic-types.md, "Which predicate, where"), the
value model is brand-blind (fz-bsx), and a ShapeId is pure layout. So the two
keys above put the SAME question of the backend, hold the SAME layout, and
compile the same instructions twice. That is the shape fz-kdt.140 and the
fz-y6w work call over-specialization: a distinction that cannot change one
emitted byte splitting a body.

SCOPE TODAY. The corpus has one brand with traffic (compiler-known `utf8`,
resolve.rs:119) and it reaches only Utf8's own boundary, so the census cost is
small; the defect is that the RULE is wrong, and it grows the moment a minting
form exists (the fz-kdt.198 owner question) and user brands acquire traffic.

SHAPE OF THE FIX. The activation key is a backend question, so it should be
keyed on the brand-ERASED type -- `erase_nominal` (or its equivalent) applied
at the key-derivation seam, not a patch inside `descr_fingerprint`, and the
same erasure the runtime predicate and `is_value_disjoint` already apply.
Red-first: the dump above holds ONE `pass/1` key, and no `--dump backend=`
output in the corpus contains a brand name (today `brand_refines_its_inner.fz`
has 29 `utf8` tokens; the other 596 fixtures have none).

CONCORDANCE: fz-kdt.198 (the encoding; its doc sentence corrected in
6e10e69f9 on wt/kdt198-refute), fz-bsx (brand-blind runtime), fz-kdt.140
(per-position specialization), the "ShapeId is pure layout" rule.
title: A brand fragments the activation key: pass/1 compiles twice for utf8(binary) and binary, one layout and one runtime test
